chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot to perform the first prayer until he had performed al-ʿAṣr. He said: “Then let him regard the prayer he performed as the first one, then let him begin al-ʿAṣr anew.”

He said: I said: If he forgot both the first prayer and al-ʿAṣr together, then remembered that at sunset? He said: “If he is still within a time in which he does not fear missing one of them, then let him perform al-Ẓuhr and then perform al-ʿAṣr. But if he fears that it will escape him, then let him begin with al-ʿAṣr and not delay it such that it passes him, lest both of them have passed him together. Rather, he should perform al-ʿAṣr within what remains of its time, then perform the first prayer after that immediately following it.”

key_terms.عَلَى أَثَرِهَا: immediately after it, in direct sequence
key_terms.غُرُوبِ ٱلشَّمْسِ: sunset, indicating the end of the prayer window under discussion
key_terms.فَوْتَ إِحْدَاهُمَا: the missing of one of the two prayers due to lack of time
key_terms.ٱلْأُولَى: the first prayer, meaning al-Ẓuhr in this context

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they forgot al-Ẓuhr until the time of al-ʿAṣr or near sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who forgets al-Ẓuhr and remembers after or near the time of al-ʿAṣr. It states that prayer order is maintained when possible, but if the remaining time is too short and there is fear of missing al-ʿAṣr, then al-ʿAṣr is performed first and al-Ẓuhr is made up immediately afterward.
